requirements.evidence: .env.example:1,7 sets APP_NAME=PegaFila / APP_LOCALE=pt_BR; phpunit.xml:22-24 pins all three; config/mail.php:111-117 sets markdown.theme 'pegafila' with themes/pegafila.css:241-247 putting #0f7490 on .button-primary; lang/pt_BR.json:559,804 add 'Reset your password' and 'Verify your email address'; routes/web.php:15-34 define all five named routes with guest group, throttle:6,1 on password.email and auth+signed+throttle on verification.verify; PasswordResetLinkController.php:31-41 always returns __('passwords.sent'); NewPasswordController.php:33-61 validates min(8)->letters()->mixedCase()->numbers() + confirmed, rotates remember_token, fires PasswordReset, redirects to '/'; VerifyEmailController uses EmailVerificationRequest (403 on id/hash mismatch). All requirements and contract items covered.

conventions.evidence: Tests ship with every behavior and docs are kept in sync (docs/ops/mail.md, README.md:27, CHANGELOG.md:12). Deviations: NewPasswordController.php:33-41 validates four fields inline where the conventions call for a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields; the two views (forgot-password.blade.php:9, reset-password.blade.php:9) load Bulma 0.9.4 from a CDN instead of the project's own Bulma build and repeat the field markup instead of using Blade components.

security.evidence: Inputs are validated server-side, there is no account enumeration (PasswordResetLinkController.php:41 gives the same response either way), throttling is applied, verification uses EmailVerificationRequest + signed, all output is escaped with {{ }} (reset-password.blade.php:22,32), and remember_token is rotated. Minor: the third-party CDN stylesheet (forgot-password.blade.php:9) has no SRI integrity attribute.

tests.evidence: PasswordResetTest covers the form, known vs unknown e-mail (same flash, nothing sent), invalid e-mail, throttle 429, a valid reset (password, remember_token, event, redirect '/'), an invalid token and a strength/confirmation dataset; EmailVerificationTest covers the URL built from the named route, the happy path, another user's id, a mismatched hash and an unsigned link; MailNotificationsTest checks the pins, the theme and the rendered pt-BR copy, including no 'having trouble clicking'. Gaps: no test that authenticated users are kept out of the guest routes, no empty-e-mail case, and the notification is only rendered via toMail() and never checked for the controller's locale.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses Laravel's Password broker, the stock notifications, EmailVerificationRequest and existing pt_BR.json entries, adding only two strings. Minor extras: PasswordResetLinkController.php:39 builds the notification by hand with ->locale('pt_BR') even though the app locale is already pt_BR (the default sendPasswordResetNotification would suffice); the two views duplicate the full HTML shell.

readability.evidence: Small, focused controllers with PHPDoc (PasswordResetLinkController.php:24-29 explains the anti-enumeration choice); clear test names; semantic, accessible markup with labels and role='alert'/'status'; no dead code or debugging leftovers.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. Small extras: User.php:15 now implements MustVerifyEmail, which the task did not ask for and which changes behavior (the Registered listener and the verified middleware); config/mail.php:112 adds a MAIL_MARKDOWN_THEME env override.

issues.explanation: Four validated fields are validated inline; the project convention asks for a Form Request once the rules grow beyond one or two fields.
Both auth views load Bulma 0.9.4 from jsDelivr instead of the project's bundled Bulma, which can drift from the app's version and styling.
The third-party CDN stylesheet on the password reset page has no integrity (SRI) attribute.
A custom callback hard-codes ->locale('pt_BR') on the notification even though APP_LOCALE already makes pt_BR the default; the broker's default sendPasswordResetNotification would be enough.

Implementing MustVerifyEmail is not required for the verification route (EmailVerificationRequest works without it) and changes registration and 'verified' middleware behavior that belongs to later tasks.
There is no test that authenticated users are redirected away from the guest-only reset routes and no empty-e-mail validation case.
The repeated Bulma field/label/help markup could be a Blade component, per the conventions.

review.summary: The change delivers the pt-BR locale pins, the pegafila mail theme with #0f7490 on the button, the two missing JSON subjects, a non-enumerating throttled password-reset flow and a signed verification route, with docs and a solid set of Pest tests. All requirements are met; the remaining points are minor: inline validation where a Form Request is expected, Bulma loaded from a CDN in standalone views, a redundant hard-coded locale, and the unrequested MustVerifyEmail interface. I would approve it with nits.
